study.title: High-throughput property-driven generative design of functional organic molecules
study.citation: Westermayr J, Gilkes J, Barrett R, Maurer RJ. Nature Computational Science 3, 139-148 (2023).
study.workflow_type: Iterative property-guided molecular generation and surrogate screening
study.assessment_scope: Published article, Supplementary Information, data and code availability statements, and linked data and code records; the analysis was not rerun.

items.summary: OE62 and the molecular filters are identified, and licence information can be recovered from linked OE62 and generated-data records. Complete split manifests, a predeclared molecular matching rule with cross-split collision rate, and shortcut and perturbation checks are not provided.
source_locations: Methods, G-SchNet model for molecule generation

items.summary: Two SchNet+H models use different random train/test splits for committee uncertainty, but split sizes, grouping rationale, model-selection use, and G-SchNet split manifests are not stated.
source_locations: Supplementary Section 3, Validation of molecules at the edges of the distributions

items.summary: The three-dimensional autoregressive representation and main G-SchNet hyperparameters are specified, including batch size 2, 10 angstrom cutoff, 128 features, nine interaction blocks, 25 Gaussian functions, and five sampled atom placements per molecule; random seeds are not stated.
source_locations: Methods, G-SchNet model for molecule generation

items.summary: The learning-rate rule, batch size, approximate loop duration, and SchNet+H hardware are reported, but final epoch counts, precision, matched training wall-clock statistics, and inference throughput are incomplete.
source_locations: Methods, G-SchNet model for molecule generation
Methods, Computational details of the workflow for targeted design

items.summary: Per-loop candidate counts, structural filtering, property-based selection thresholds, retraining, and the 70-atom restriction introduced for ionisation-potential generation are stated.
source_locations: Methods, Computational details of the workflow for targeted design

items.summary: Property distributions, valid molecule counts, diversity analyses, committee disagreement, and higher-level electronic-structure checks are reported, but a formal novelty definition, one stagewise metric record, and uncertainty across independent generative runs are absent.
source_locations: Supplementary Sections 1-4, Supplementary Figs. 1-11, and Supplementary Data 1

items.summary: Knockout experiments and comparisons between single- and multi-property biasing are included, but no matched random, retrieval, virtual-screening, or simple non-deep-learning baseline receives the same evaluator budget.
source_locations: Main text, Results, Analysis of the generative model

items.summary: SCScore is defined and applied as a synthetic-complexity proxy from canonical SMILES, but retrosynthesis settings, a route-level success criterion, and experimental synthesis validation are not included.
source_locations: Methods, SCScore to predict the complexity of synthesizability of molecules

items.summary: Generated data, calculations, modified code releases, archived versions, and tutorials are linked, but no environment lockfile, split checksums, complete determinism record, or one-command rebuild is identified.

Iterative thresholds, two-model committee uncertainty, loop counts, and a qualitative stopping rule are described, but the stopping tolerance is not numerical and the complete evaluator budget is not consolidated.
source_locations: Methods, Computational details of the workflow for targeted design

items.summary: Approximate loop and training times and the CPU and GPU systems are reported; candidate-throughput uncertainty and energy or carbon estimates are not.
source_locations: Methods, Computational details of the workflow for targeted design

items.summary: The study targets electronic properties of small organic molecules and does not expose a hazardous target, autonomous execution pathway, or access mechanism that makes a governance control material to the reported claim. Dataset and code licences are assessed under D1 and R1.
source_locations: Main article, Workflow, Data availability, and Code availability

items.summary: Candidate counts, valid counts, loop numbers, validation subsets, and approximate compute are available, but are distributed across the article, Supplementary Information, and Supplementary Data.
source_locations: Methods, Computational details of the workflow for targeted design

notes: This is a disclosure audit rather than a methodological quality score. No unreported detail was inferred.
